messages:
sanjay: ran a 6h perf sweep on the vector/rerank endpoints this morning. noticed intermittent p99 spikes during arrival bursts (~+2-3x) even though overall throughput stayed flat. suspect continuous batcher heuristics + token budget targeting.

maggie: can you paste the quick numbers and which nodes?

sanjay: staging cluster v3-gpu-24, mixed small/large vectors. summary: p50 ~28ms (stable), p95 92ms -> unchanged, p99 jumped from ~180ms to ~420ms when queue_depth > 120. overall TPS steady. KV cache hit rate dipped from 92% -> 85% during the spike (likely short-lived prefixes causing cache churn). profiler shows more small-kernel fallbacks during those windows (kernel_selector logged more "matmul_small_block" choices).

riley: interesting. sounds like batch formation is creating a lot of oversize batches that push token budgets over the target and force fallback kernels. did you capture batching metrics?

sanjay: yes, attached snippet from the batcher trace (trimmed):
```
window_ms: 12 -> samples show many 1-3 item batches collapsing into 48-96 item batches in a single tick
avg_batch_tokens: 180 -> spikes to 950 during bursts
token_budget_target: 0.75
queue_len: spike to 160
```
we also logged kernel latencies: matmul_small_block 10-30ms/item vs int8-gemm 4-8ms/item. once we hit >800 tokens batch, kernel_selector avoids int8 path.

tia: for vector-only (non-chat) traffic we should bias for item-count fairness rather than token-budget strictness. small requests (<=64 tokens) are high QPS and get starved otherwise. propose: lower token_budget_target and smaller max_batch_items for vector endpoints.

riley: i agree — propose quick config to test on staging:
```yaml
queue_policy:
  max_batch_items: 32
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
  token_budget_target: 0.6
  window_ms: 6
  min_batch_delay_ms: 2
```
this should stop the 60-100 item bursts and let kernel_selector stay on the fast int8 path.

maggie: does that cost us throughput? and what about tail for large vector requests?

sanjay: ran that exact config for 2h on staging. results: p99 dropped to ~210ms during similar synthetic spikes (was 420ms), aggregate throughput -1.8%, KV hit recovered to ~90%. large single-shot requests >2000 tokens saw a small latency increase (~+10ms) but still within SLA.

eng-bot: deploy: rollout staged -> applied config to staging cluster "vec-staging-3" at 1763112600 by riley (canary 10%) :rocket:

tia: nice. next step: A/B in prod with a conservative ramp and a capacity cap so we can fallback. A/B plan: 10% traffic -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 4 hours, monitor p99, KV hit, kernel_choice ratio. fallback: if p99 > 2x baseline or KV hit < 80% rollback.

riley: i'll add the rollout recipe to the console (canary route + capacity_takeover fallback) and add a perf-harness test to reproduce the exact queue spike shape.

maggie: please also add a small alert on kernel_selector_fallback_rate metric so SRE notices if int8 path loss increases >5% over baseline.

sanjay: noted. I'll push a short-lived dashboard with these charts and the trace links. TL;DR: change token_budget_target 0.75->0.6, shrink max_batch_items to 32, window_ms 12->6 for vector endpoints; staging numbers look good. Rollout plan above.

riley: I'll schedule the prod canary tomorrow morning 0900 PT. tagging @tia for runbook check. :eyes:

tia: runbook looks fine. will be on-call during the rollout.

maggie: great work — thanks team. small doc follow-up: please add reason (kernel selection fallback) to the change note so PMs understand perf tradeoffs. :+1:
